subject: errors with estimator WLSMV with ordered factors

messages.author: 31574c2c748090f9
messages.subject: errors with estimator WLSMV with ordered factors
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to run the following model, where N_cat and ants_bin are ordered factors (with 3 and 2 levels, respectively), the rest of the variables are continuous (numeric):

path.model6<-'aphids.p.biomass~N_cat+ants_bin
            avg_HI~N_cat+ants_bin
            Flowers~N_cat+ants_bin+aphids.p.biomass+avg_HI'
path.fit6<-cfa(path.model6, data=data, estimator="WLSMV")

I get the following error + warnings, no matter which slight variant of the path model I try:
Error in crossprod(Delta[[g]], lavsamp...@WLS.VD[[g]] * diff) : 
  non-conformable arguments
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :
  lavaan WARNING: exogenous variable(s) declared as ordered in data: N_cat ants_bin
2: In muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]], ov.types = ov.types,  :
  lavaan WARNING: trouble inverting W matrix; used generalized inverse
3: In WLS.obs - WLS.est :
  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length
4: In lavsamp...@WLS.obs[[g]] - WLS.est[[g]] :
  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length

If I label only call one of the factors ordered (doesn't matter which one), I get:
Error in muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]], ov.types = ov.types,  : 
  unknown ov.types:factor
plus warnings about the exogenous variables being ordered (or unordered when N_cat with 3 levels is not ordered)

If I label both variables as factors, model runs fine and exhibits expected behaviors with estimator = "MLM"

Any idea where the problem(s) is/are?

Many thanks,

Beth

messages.author: 31574c2c748090f9
messages.subject: Re: errors with estimator WLSMV with ordered factors
parts:
Hi again,

I guess my question boils down to whether I need to be worried about interpreting the model output if I consider what could be ordered data as unordered factors instead, running a cfa model with estimator = MLM. Both factors are exogenous variables, and all endogenous variables are continuous.

Thanks very much,

Beth

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: errors with estimator WLSMV with ordered factors
parts:
You might solve your problem by turning your three-category variable into two dichotomous variables.  Then your exogenous variables would all be dichotomous.  If treating them as ordered factors doesn't work, and treating them as unordered factors doesn't work, treat them as numeric, and that should work fine.
     For certain, an unordered factor with three categories will cause substantial problems.
--Ed Rigdon
